overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the main forecasts about advanced AI and what divides them. You'll be asked about the catastrophic-risk position, the abundance position, the normal-technology position and the skeptics, and the assumptions and survey evidence on which the forecasts diverge.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What kind of evidence does the catastrophic-risk position rest on?

options.html: Documented cases of AI systems escaping human control in real use
options.text: Documented cases of AI systems escaping human control in real use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. There is no observed case of an AI system escaping human control. The position rests on argument and laboratory findings.

options.html: Argument and laboratory findings, with no observed case so far
options.text: Argument and laboratory findings, with no observed case so far
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The position combines an argument about capable systems with hard-to-set goals and tests in constructed scenarios. No real-world case has been observed.

options.html: A survey result that measures the true probability of extinction
options.text: A survey result that measures the true probability of extinction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A survey reports researchers' guesses and doesn't measure the risk. The position rests on argument and laboratory findings.

options.html: Historical records of earlier technologies that could not be corrected
options.text: Historical records of earlier technologies that could not be corrected
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Historical analogy is the main support for the normal-technology position. The catastrophic-risk position rests on argument and laboratory findings.

forms.stemHtml: Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, wrote a 2024 essay forecasting large benefits from AI and a 2026 essay about its dangers. What does this show about the abundance and catastrophic-risk positions?

options.html: The two positions are held by entirely separate groups of people
options.text: The two positions are held by entirely separate groups of people
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The same author wrote both essays and signed the 2023 statement on extinction risk. The positions overlap, and some people hold both as possibilities.

options.html: The abundance position was withdrawn once the dangers became clear
options.text: The abundance position was withdrawn once the dangers became clear
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The 2026 essay doesn't retract the earlier forecast. The positions overlap, and some people hold both as possibilities.

options.html: Forecasts by company leaders can be set aside as mere marketing
options.text: Forecasts by company leaders can be set aside as mere marketing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A commercial stake is a reason to check an argument, not proof that it's false. The point here is that the positions overlap, and some people hold both as possibilities.

options.html: The positions overlap, and some people hold both as possibilities
options.text: The positions overlap, and some people hold both as possibilities
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Abundance and catastrophe aren't opposite camps. Several prominent figures write about large benefits and serious risks together.

forms.stemHtml: In "AI as Normal Technology," what do Narayanan and Kapoor mean by "normal"?

options.html: A tool of the same kind as electricity, spreading over decades
options.text: A tool of the same kind as electricity, spreading over decades
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They say the term doesn't understate AI's impact. It places AI with earlier transformative technologies that people kept under control.

options.html: A minor technology whose effects on society will be small ones
options.text: A minor technology whose effects on society will be small ones
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors say their view doesn't understate AI's impact. They mean a tool of the same kind as electricity, spreading over decades.

options.html: A technology that carries no serious risks for anyone to manage
options.text: A technology that carries no serious risks for anyone to manage
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors discuss risks such as inequality and concentration of power. They mean a tool of the same kind as electricity, spreading over decades.

options.html: A technology that will soon match humans and then level off there
options.text: A technology that will soon match humans and then level off there
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors make no such claim. They mean a tool of the same kind as electricity, spreading over decades.

forms.stemHtml: A 2023 survey of 2,778 AI researchers produced median estimates of 5 or 10 percent for outcomes as bad as human extinction. Which statements about this result are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The median answer changed with the wording of the question
options.text: The median answer changed with the wording of the question
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a framing effect. Different versions of the question produced medians of 5 and 10 percent.

options.html: It shows that many AI researchers take the risk seriously
options.text: It shows that many AI researchers take the risk seriously
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is what the survey is good evidence of.

options.html: It measures the actual probability that AI will cause extinction
options.text: It measures the actual probability that AI will cause extinction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Respondents were guessing about systems that don't exist. The survey reports opinion and isn't a measurement of the risk.

options.html: Only about 15 percent of the researchers invited responded
options.text: Only about 15 percent of the researchers invited responded
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A low response rate means those who answered may differ from those who didn't.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers who doubt that AI will rapidly accelerate its own development point to computing power. What is their argument?

options.html: Computing power is now so cheap that it no longer affects research
options.text: Computing power is now so cheap that it no longer affects research
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The argument is the reverse. If ideas must be tested in large experiments, computing power may be a bottleneck that more researchers can't remove.

options.html: AI systems are unable to write code that improves other AI systems
options.text: AI systems are unable to write code that improves other AI systems
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. AI systems already help with parts of AI research. The argument is that computing power may be a bottleneck that more researchers can't remove.

options.html: It may be a bottleneck that more researchers can't remove
options.text: It may be a bottleneck that more researchers can't remove
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If new ideas have to be tested in large, costly experiments, adding researchers, human or AI, doesn't speed progress much without more computing power.

options.html: Governments have already capped the computing power labs may use
options.text: Governments have already capped the computing power labs may use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The argument isn't about regulation. It is that computing power may be a bottleneck that more researchers can't remove.

title: Forecasts in conflict: catastrophe, abundance, and normal technology
